text: What does a ribosome make directly when it translates an mRNA molecule?
options: a folded enzyme made of several chains
a DNA copy of the gene
solution: Translation joins amino acids in the order set by the codons, making a polypeptide chain: the primary structure. Folding into the final 3-D shape, and joining with other chains, happens afterwards and is not the direct product. mRNA comes from transcription.

text: Which one of the following lies in the thorax, ABOVE the diaphragm, in a human?
solution: The diaphragm separates the thorax (heart, lungs, thymus, the lower trachea) from the abdomen. The thymus sits in front of the heart, in the chest. The stomach, spleen, kidneys and pancreas are all abdominal organs below the diaphragm.

text: Which one of the following contains NO nucleotides?
solution: Cellulose is a polysaccharide of glucose. Ribosomes contain rRNA, chromosomes contain DNA, every virus has DNA or RNA, and ATP is itself a nucleotide (adenine, ribose and three phosphates).

text: Which statement about mitochondria is NOT correct?
options: Mitochondria are the site of the Krebs cycle.
solution: Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm; only its product, pyruvate, enters the mitochondrion. Everything else is true: two membranes (the inner one folded into cristae), a small circular DNA, their own small ribosomes, and the Krebs cycle in the matrix.

text:
One strand of a short piece of DNA reads TGC-CAT-AGG.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1 The other strand includes the triplet ACG.
2 Each of the three triplets is held to the other strand by 8 hydrogen bonds.
3 If this strand is the template, the mRNA made from it contains 2 uracil bases.
solution: 1: TGC pairs with ACG. 2: A-T pairs have 2 hydrogen bonds and G-C pairs 3. TGC has 2 + 3 + 3 = 8, but CAT has 3 + 2 + 2 = 7, so not all three have 8. 3: the mRNA is ACG-GUA-UCC, with 2 uracils. So 1 and 3 only.

text: Which one of the following is NOT part of the body's defence against pathogens?
options: mucus and cilia in the trachea
solution: Red blood cells carry oxygen and have no defensive role. Mucus traps microbes and cilia sweep them away, stomach acid kills many that are swallowed, lysozyme breaks down bacterial walls, and a clot seals a wound so pathogens cannot get in.

text:
In which stages of aerobic respiration is reduced NAD produced?
1 glycolysis
2 the link reaction
3 the Krebs cycle
4 oxidative phosphorylation
solution: NAD is reduced in glycolysis, in the link reaction (pyruvate to acetyl coenzyme A) and several times in the Krebs cycle. Oxidative phosphorylation does the opposite: it oxidises reduced NAD back to \(\mathrm{NAD^+}\), passing its electrons along the chain to oxygen.

text:
In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 21% of the bases are adenine.
What percentage of the bases are cytosine?
solution: A pairs with T, so thymine is also 21%, and A + T = 42%. The remaining 58% is G + C, split equally because G pairs with C: cytosine is 29%. 58 is G and C together.

text: Which stage of mitosis comes immediately BEFORE anaphase?
solution: The order is prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, followed by cytokinesis; interphase comes between divisions. Metaphase, when the chromosomes line up at the equator, comes just before anaphase, when the chromatids are pulled apart.

text:
The frequency of an allele in a small population of beetles changes over several generations.
Which of the following could cause this?
1 genetic drift
2 natural selection
3 beetles from another population moving in and breeding
solution: Allele frequencies change by chance (genetic drift, strongest in small populations), when some alleles help survival and reproduction (natural selection), and when individuals bring in alleles from elsewhere (gene flow by migration). All three.

text: Which molecule is USED UP in photosynthesis and PRODUCED by aerobic respiration?
solution: Photosynthesis fixes carbon dioxide into sugar, and respiration releases it again. Oxygen and glucose go the other way round: made in photosynthesis, used in respiration. Reduced NADP belongs to photosynthesis only, and chlorophyll is not used up.

text:
A plant cell is seen in metaphase of mitosis.
Which of these features could be used, at this moment, to show that it is eukaryotic rather than prokaryotic?
1 a cell wall
2 chloroplasts
3 a nuclear envelope
solution: Chloroplasts are membrane-bound organelles, found only in eukaryotes. Many prokaryotes also have a cell wall, so a wall proves nothing. And during metaphase the nuclear envelope has broken down, so it cannot be seen. 2 only.

chapter: States of Matter and Gas Laws
text: Which statement about changes of state is NOT correct?
options: Melting absorbs energy from the surroundings.
Condensation releases energy to the surroundings.
Sublimation is a solid turning directly into a gas.
The boiling point of a liquid depends on the surrounding pressure.
Evaporation can only happen at the boiling point.
solution: Evaporation happens from a liquid's surface at any temperature (puddles dry at 20 °C); boiling is evaporation throughout the liquid, at the temperature where vapour pressure equals the surrounding pressure. The other statements are correct.

text:
Ethanal can be made from ethene in three steps:
\[\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2} \xrightarrow{1\ (\mathrm{HBr})} \mathrm{CH_3CH_2Br} \xrightarrow{2\ (\mathrm{NaOH(aq)})} \mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH} \xrightarrow{3\ (\mathrm{acidified\ K_2Cr_2O_7})} \mathrm{CH_3CHO}\]
Which types of reaction are steps 1, 2 and 3?
solution: 1: HBr adds across the C=C double bond (addition). 2: hydroxide replaces the bromine (nucleophilic substitution). 3: dichromate removes hydrogen from the alcohol, turning it into an aldehyde (oxidation).

text:
Which of the following must be true of two compounds in the same homologous series?
1 They fit the same general formula.
2 They have the same functional group.
3 They have the same boiling point.
solution: A homologous series shares a general formula (such as \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}OH}\) for alcohols) and a functional group, so its members have similar chemical properties. Each member adds a \(\mathrm{CH_2}\), so physical properties such as boiling point change steadily along the series. 1 and 2 only.

text:
Which of the following statements about the double bond in ethene is/are correct?
1 It is shorter than the C-C single bond in ethane.
2 It is made of one sigma bond and one pi bond.
3 It prevents rotation of one end of the molecule relative to the other.
solution: Four shared electrons pull the carbons closer, so C=C is shorter than C-C (1). The double bond is a sigma bond along the axis plus a pi bond above and below it (2). Twisting would break the sideways pi overlap, so rotation is restricted, which is why alkenes can have cis-trans isomers (3). All three.

text:
Here are some compounds of sulfur:
\(\mathrm{H_2S} \quad \mathrm{SO_2} \quad \mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3} \quad \mathrm{SO_3} \quad \mathrm{H_2SO_4}\)
Which list gives exactly the oxidation numbers shown by sulfur in these compounds? (In \(\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3}\), take both sulfur atoms as equal.)

Potassium manganate(VII) oxidises concentrated hydrochloric acid to chlorine:
\[2\mathrm{KMnO_4} + a\,\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{KCl} + 2\mathrm{MnCl_2} + b\,\mathrm{Cl_2} + c\,\mathrm{H_2O}\]
What must \(c\) be for the equation to balance?
solution: Balance oxygen first: 2 \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) have 8 O, all ending in water, so \(c = 8\). Then hydrogen: 16 H in water means \(a = 16\). Chlorine: 16 on the left, and 2 (KCl) + 4 (\(\mathrm{MnCl_2}\)) = 6 on the right, leaving 10 Cl as 5 \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\). 16 is \(a\) and 5 is \(b\).

text:
How many oxygen atoms are in 88 g of carbon dioxide?
[Relative atomic masses: C = 12; O = 16; Avogadro constant = \(6.0 \times 10^{23}\ \mathrm{mol^{-1}}\)]
solution: \(M_r\) of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) = 44, so 88 g is 2.0 mol of molecules. Each has two O atoms: 4.0 mol of O atoms = \(4.0 \times 6.0 \times 10^{23} = 2.4 \times 10^{24}\). \(1.2 \times 10^{24}\) is the number of molecules.

subject: Physics
text:
A simple pendulum swings to and fro with a small amplitude.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1 The bob moves fastest at the lowest point of its swing.
2 The bob's acceleration is zero at each end of its swing.
3 The bob's gravitational potential energy is greatest at each end of its swing.
solution: Energy moves between kinetic and potential: the bob is highest (most potential energy) at the ends and lowest, and fastest, in the middle. At the ends it stops for an instant, but the restoring force, and so the acceleration, is at its LARGEST there; acceleration is zero at the centre. 1 and 3 only.

subject: Mathematics
text: A circle has centre (2, -3) and radius 4. Which of the following is its equation?
solution: \((x - 2)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 16\) expands to \(x^2 - 4x + 4 + y^2 + 6y + 9 = 16\), so \(x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 6y - 3 = 0\). Wrong signs on \(4x\) and \(6y\) put the centre at (-2, 3), and forgetting the 4 + 9 gives the -16 version.

subject: Physics
text:
In these expressions, \(F\) = force, \(s\) = distance, \(m\) = mass, \(v\) = velocity, \(P\) = power, \(t\) = time, \(I\) = current and \(R\) = resistance.
Which of them have the unit of energy?
1 \(Fs\)
2 \(\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2\)
3 \(\dfrac{P}{t}\)
4 \(I^2Rt\)
solution: Force x distance is work, in joules. \(\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2\) is kinetic energy: kg m²/s² = J. \(I^2R\) is electrical power, so \(I^2Rt\) is energy. Power DIVIDED by time is J/s², not energy; power TIMES time would be.

subject: Mathematics
text:
Simplify
\[\log\frac{x^3}{2} + \log\frac{4}{x} - \log 2x\]
solution: Adding logs multiplies and subtracting divides: \(\log\left(\dfrac{x^3}{2} \times \dfrac{4}{x} \div 2x\right) = \log\dfrac{4x^3}{4x^2} = \log x\). A sum of logs is never the log of a sum.

subject: Mathematics
text: For which values of \(x\) are both \(x^2 - 9 < 0\) and \(3x - 2 \geq 4\) true?
solution: \(x^2 < 9\) means \(-3 < x < 3\) (strict, so 3 is excluded). \(3x \geq 6\) means \(x \geq 2\) (2 included). Both together: \(2 \leq x < 3\).
